# CBDB-Desktop: Places form revisions, 2026-10-14

Found while writing the Places (Look At Place) section of the user's guide, not from an automated-testing report, so these entries have no CBDB-D numbers yet. Assign numbers as needed. Changes are in Code/places_form_backend.go and the form's index.html. They were compiled and checked with test queries; the export functions are still to be tested.

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLC-1 | The Aggregated tab only kept the first record for each person + address + category, hiding other relations and associates | New aggregateRecords() combines each group and marks multiple relations or associates | Tested |
| PLC-2 | The Aggregated tab had no Chinese relation column | 關係 (relChn) column added | Tested |
| PLC-3 | The Kinship branch read ASSOC_DATA (the kin intermediary of an association) instead of KIN_DATA | Branch rewritten to read KIN_DATA | Compiled, tested |
| PLC-4 | The People tab showed the place that matched the query, not the person's index address | Index address fields added to each record; People tab uses them | Compiled, tested |
| PLC-5 | The people file in Export Query Results had the same fault as PLC-4 | People file uses the index address fields; full record file gains them as extra columns | Compiled; export not yet tested |

## PLC-1: Aggregated tab rules

**Issue.** renderAggTable deduplicated on person + address + category (relType) and kept the first record of each group. When a group held several relations, or the same relation with several associates, only one was shown, with nothing to say others existed.

**Fix.** A new function, aggregateRecords() in index.html, groups the records the same way and produces one row per group:

| Group contains | Relation | 關係 |
|---|---|---|
| More than one relation | Multiple | 多項 |
| One relation, more than one associate | relation + " [Multiple]" | relation + "[多]" |
| One relation, one associate (possibly several records) | unchanged | unchanged |

The first rule takes precedence, so a group with several relations and several associates shows "Multiple".

Details:

- Relations are compared by relCode, not relDesc, because different codes can share a description. For example, two offices can have the same c_office_trans, and some translations are blank.
- Associates are compared by assocId, except for the Institution category. Institution rows carry the institution name in assocName and set assocId to 0, so they are compared by assocName.
- All other fields come from the first record in the group. Groups keep first-seen order, so the unsorted display order is unchanged.
- renderAggTable calls aggregateRecords() in place of its old dedup loop.

Rows with several records but the same relation and associate (for example, different years or sources) are shown once, unchanged.

**For the user's guide.** The Aggregated tab is computed in the browser. Export Query Results still writes the raw records (PlacePeopleRecords.tsv), not the aggregated rows. See Open items.

## PLC-2: Chinese relation column on the Aggregated tab

The Aggregated tab's column list (TAB_COLUMNS.agg) and renderAggTable now include relChn (header 關係) after Relation. It is sortable like the other text columns. The omission was an oversight.

## PLC-3: Kinship branch used the wrong table

**Symptom.** Found by code review. Branch 5 (Kinship) selected from ASSOC_DATA WHERE c_kin_code &gt; 0. In ASSOC_DATA, c_kin_code and c_kin_id identify the kin intermediary of an association (the relative through whom the association was made), not a kinship tie. So the branch returned associations made through a relative, labelled with that intermediary's kinship relation, and assocId held the associate, not a relative.

**Fix.** The branch now reads KIN_DATA:

| Output column | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Source table | ASSOC_DATA AD | KIN_DATA KD |
| rel_code | AD.c_kin_code | KD.c_kin_code |
| assoc_id | AD.c_assoc_id | KD.c_kin_id |
| Associate (BM2) join | AD.c_assoc_id | KD.c_kin_id |
| source | AD.c_source | KD.c_source |
| Filter | AD.c_kin_code &gt; 0 | KD.c_kin_id &gt; 0 |

The address filter is still applied to the second person's index address (BM2.c_index_addr_id). A person is therefore included when one of their relatives has an index address in the selected place(s), the same pattern as Branch 3 (Associate's Index Place). The c_kin_id &gt; 0 filter excludes relatives recorded as [Unknown] (person 0). rel_type stays 'Kinship', so the UCINet export still marks these edges as K.

**Access version.** The VBA Kinship query in LookAtPlace also reads KIN_DATA. It joins the relative (KIN_DATA.c_kin_id) to BIOG_MAIN and filters on the relative's c_index_addr_id. Its output columns match the new Go branch, so this fix brings the Go version into line with the original; the ASSOC_DATA version was a porting error. Two small differences remain, both reviewed and accepted:

- The VBA joins KINSHIP_CODES with an INNER JOIN where Go uses a LEFT JOIN. Referential integrity is enforced between KIN_DATA and KINSHIP_CODES, so the two give the same rows.
- The VBA has no c_kin_id &gt; 0 filter. KIN_DATA rows with c_kin_id = 0 carry no useful information, and data editors have been told to delete them. The VBA has worked without the filter, but the Go version keeps it as a safeguard.

**For the user's guide.** Kinship results show where a person's relatives have their index addresses, not where the person lived. Relatives with no index address in ADDR_CODES do not appear.

## PLC-4: People tab used the matched place instead of the index address

**Symptom.** The People tab takes one record per person and showed its addrName, addrChn, X, Y and XYCount. Those fields describe the place that matched the query, which differs by branch: the posting location for Office Place, the relative's index address for Kinship, and so on. The tab therefore showed whichever matched place happened to come first. Its Chinese header was 指數地址 ("index address"), which shows the intended meaning.

**Cause.** handleQuery returned IndexAddrID but none of the index address's name or coordinates, so the front end had nothing else to show.

**Fix (back end).**

- PlaceRecord has five new fields: IndexAddrName, IndexAddrChn, IndexAddrX, IndexAddrY (JSON indexAddrName, indexAddrChn, indexAddrX, indexAddrY) and IndexXYCount (JSON indexXYCount). The coordinates are pointers, so a missing value comes through as null rather than 0.
- A new method, fillIndexAddresses, runs after the query. It looks up all distinct index addresses in ADDR_CODES with one query, rather than adding a join to each of the seven branches, and fills the four address fields. Index address 0 is left blank.
- IndexXYCount is the number of distinct people in the result set whose index addresses have the same coordinates. Each person is counted once however many records they have. The existing XYCount still counts result records at the matched place and is still used on the other two tabs.
- A failure in fillIndexAddresses is logged and does not stop the query; the index address fields are then blank.

**Fix (front end).** TAB_COLUMNS.people and renderPeopleTable now show Index Address, 指數地址, X, Y and XYCount from the new fields.

## PLC-5: Export Query Results people file

**Issue.** placeWriteResultsPeopleTab (PlacePeopleRecordsPeople.tsv) used the same matched-place fields as the People tab, so it had the same fault as PLC-4.

**Fix.**

- PlacePeopleRecordsPeople.tsv now writes IndexAddrID, IndexAddrName, IndexAddrChn, IndexAddrX, IndexAddrY and IndexXYCount in place of AddrName, AddrChn, XCoord, YCoord and XYCount.
- PlacePeopleRecords.tsv (the full record dump) keeps all its columns and adds IndexAddrName, IndexAddrChn, IndexAddrX, IndexAddrY and IndexXYCount at the end.

## Decisions recorded

- **Institution coordinates.** The VBA Institution query takes X and Y from SOCIAL_INSTITUTION_ADDR (inst_xcoord, inst_ycoord); the Go branch takes them from ADDR_CODES for the institution's address (c_inst_addr_id). No institution has yet needed its own coordinates, and any difference would be a few kilometres at most, so the address coordinates are kept for now. inst_xcoord and inst_ycoord may be used in future.

## Not affected

- The Place–People Records tab is unchanged; its address columns are still the matched place, which is correct for that tab.
- The Neo4j export already took index addresses from IndexAddrID and looks up their names itself, so PLC-4 does not change it.
- No schema changes were needed.
